title: Are forests wilderness?
body: What distinguishes the forest movements of the South from those of the North is that the forests of the South are still peopled, while the forests of the North are more or less devoid of human habitat, or are at least perceived that way. In the North, wilderness is often seen as a 'wild place' where people do not live, and the environment is treated as something 'out there' that must be protected from humans by creating parks and reserves. Wilderness-oriented perspectives have been strongest in Australia, Scandinavia, North America and New Zealand. Wilderness campaigns are not missing in the South: groups in the Philippines protect eagles and other birds of prey, campaigners in India work to protect the Bengal tiger, and in Africa a long campaign has been waged against the ivory trade. Many such campaigns, often funded by NGOs such as the WWF together with local people, have in recent times been renamed biodiversity campaigns.
